title: Central torus quotient in relative semisimple rank one
statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. An $S$-group scheme is a group object in schemes over $S$, with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] over this base. A reductive $S$-group means a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] affine finite-type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] $S$-group all of whose geometric fibres are connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] and have no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent closed subgroup. Unipotent means that every geometric point is unipotent in a faithful matrix representation. A split maximal torus $T\hookrightarrow G$ is a closed subgroup [def-weil-closed-immersion] isomorphic to $\mathbf G_{m,S}^r$, $r\geq0$, maximal among tori on every geometric fibre; a torus over an algebraically closed field is a product of multiplicative groups. Here $\mathbf G_{m,S}=\operatorname{Spec}A[z,z^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units. Semisimple rank one means that the quotient of each geometric fibre by its largest smooth connected normal solvable subgroup has maximal tori of dimension one; solvable means that successive scheme-theoretic commutator subgroups become trivial. The centre is the subgroup functor of points commuting with every point after every algebra extension. Let $G$ be reductive with split maximal torus $T=\operatorname{Spec}A[M]$, $M=\mathbf Z^r$, and semisimple rank one. For $m\in M$, write $\chi_m(z)=z^m$ and let $\mathfrak g_m$ be its weight summand in the conjugation action on the tangent module $\operatorname{Lie}(G)$, with the full coaction meaning of [lem-sfb-relative-tangent-weight-base-change]. Suppose $\alpha\in M\setminus\{0\}$ is a root on every geometric fibre. Write $\alpha=d\alpha_0$ with $d>0$ and $\alpha_0$ primitive, meaning $M/\mathbf Z\alpha_0$ is torsion-free. Then $r\geq1$, $d\in\{1,2\}$, the only nonzero fibre roots are $\alpha,-\alpha$, and $Z(G)=\ker\chi_\alpha$ as subgroup schemes of $T$. The subgroup $K=\ker\chi_{\alpha_0}=D_A(M/\mathbf Z\alpha_0)$ [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group] is a central split torus of rank $r-1$. The fppf sheaf quotient $H=G/K$ is represented by a reductive $S$-group; fppf sheaf quotient means the sheafification of $U\mapsto G(U)/K(U)$ for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings. The quotient map is a $K$-torsor: it is faithfully flat of finite presentation and $(g,k)\mapsto(g,gk)$ identifies $G\times_S K$ with $G\times_H G$. The subgroup $\overline T=T/K\simeq\mathbf G_{m,S}$ is a split maximal torus in $H$, its inverse image in $G$ is exactly $T$, and $H$ has semisimple rank one with centre $Z(H)=Z(G)/K\simeq\mu_{d,S}$. Here $\mu_{d,S}=\operatorname{Spec}A[t]/(t^d-1)$ with multiplication, so it is finite locally free of rank $d$, and $\mu_{1,S}$ is trivial. These subgroup and quotient identifications commute with arbitrary base change.

source.place: Conrad, Theorem 3.3.4, Corollaries 3.3.5--3.3.6, printed pp.97--101; Theorem 5.1.8, first paragraph of proof, printed p.139; saturated root sublattice and centre of the central-torus quotient. proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-split-rank-one-classification] to each geometric fibre and its given maximal torus. In the three matrix models, diagonal conjugation on an upper off-diagonal tangent matrix has character respectively $t^2$, $t$, or $t_1/t_2$; the lower off-diagonal character is its inverse and all other weights are zero. Thus the roots are $\{\alpha,-\alpha\}$ on every fibre. Divisibility in $M$ is invariant under a change of torus coordinates, so the displayed characters give $d=2,1,1$, respectively. Since $\alpha\ne0$, $r\ge1$.

source.place: Theorem 5.1.8, opening proof, printed p.139; fibrewise matrix calculation using the existing field classification.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-relative-reductive-centre-weight-kernel] with the constant nonzero fibre-weight set $\Phi=\{\alpha,-\alpha\}$. It gives, over $A$ itself and scheme-theoretically, $Z(G)=D_A(M/\mathbf Z\alpha)=\ker\chi_\alpha$. This does not infer an equality of closed subschemes merely from their geometric fibres.

source.place: Theorem 3.3.4, proof, and Corollary 3.3.6(1), printed pp.99--101.

proof.text: The coordinates of primitive $\alpha_0$ have gcd one: otherwise $M/\mathbf Z\alpha_0$ has torsion. Integer elementary row operations from the Euclidean algorithm carry this vector to $(1,0,\ldots,0)$. In those coordinates $\chi_{\alpha_0}(z)=z_1$ and $\chi_\alpha(z)=z_1^d$. Thus $K=\{z_1=1\}\simeq\mathbf G_m^{r-1}$ lies in $Z(G)$. Character duality [lem-sfb-relative-diagonalizable-character-duality] gives $K=D_A(M/\mathbf Z\alpha_0)$ and $T/K=D_A(\mathbf Z\alpha_0)\simeq\mathbf G_m$.

source.place: Theorem 5.1.8, first paragraph of proof, printed p.139; Appendix B.1 for character duality.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-central-multiplicative-quotient] to this central split torus $K$. It gives the represented reductive $H$, the $K$-torsor map, the maximal torus $\overline T=T/K$ with inverse image $T$, and $Z(H)=Z(G)/K$. Character duality identifies the last quotient with $D_A(\mathbf Z\alpha_0/\mathbf Z\alpha)=D_A(\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z)\simeq\mu_{d,S}$. Its coordinate algebra $A[t]/(t^d-1)$ has basis $1,t,\ldots,t^{d-1}$, so it is finite locally free of rank $d$; for $d=1$ it is trivial.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.5, printed pp.100--101; Appendix B.1; Theorem 5.1.8, opening proof, printed p.139.

proof.text: On each geometric fibre, the radical of $H$ is its largest central torus by [lem-sfb-reductive-radical-quotient]. Such a torus in $Z(H)=\mu_d$ is trivial: character duality makes a map from a split torus to $\mu_d$ a homomorphism from $\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z$ to a torsion-free lattice, necessarily zero. Hence $H$ is semisimple on every geometric fibre, and its one-dimensional maximal torus gives semisimple rank one. The centre and quotient theorems and character duality all commute with arbitrary base change. Their kernel, torsor and inverse-image identifications therefore persist after every base change; the equations $z_1=1$, $z_1^d=1$ and the displayed monic basis do too.

The two new nodes lem-sfb-relative-central-multiplicative-quotient and lem-sfb-relative-reductive-centre-weight-kernel defined a maximal torus only as a closed subgroup that is a maximal torus on every geometric fibre. That makes their general clauses false. Counterexample: A=k[eps], G=G_m and H=Spec A[z^{±1}]/(eps(z-1)), a Hopf ideal, give a non-flat closed subgroup whose geometric fibre is G_m, yet Z(G)=G is not contained in H. Both statements now require the maximal torus to be a torus over S (fppf-locally G_m^n) as well as fibrewise maximal, which is Conrad's definition; only the statement field changed. The item uses only split T≅G_m^r, which meets the corrected definition, so its steps are unaffected. Item: statement unchanged, five steps checked. Step 1: the field classification hypotheses match, fibre characters are M, and the root sets ±(0,2), ±(0,1), ±(e1-e2) give d=2,1,1 with fixed alpha. Step 2: the centre node with Phi={±alpha} gives Z=D(M/Z alpha). Step 3: a GL_r(Z) basis change gives K={z1=1}, contained in Z(G). Step 4: the quotient node plus duality with N=M/Z alpha and L=Z alpha0/Z alpha give Z(H)=D(Z/d)=mu_d. Step 5: the radical-quotient node on fibres, with mu_d containing no torus, gives semisimple rank one. Small cases checked: SL2 (including the non-reduced mu_2 in characteristic 2), PGL2, GL2 and r=1; for the new nodes, Phi empty, C=1 and SL2/mu2. A whole-DAG search found only field versions and other relative statements, so there are no duplicates. Neither new node restates a clause of the item.
